answer: The orchard multiplier is published, charged in marble, and glacier lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3840 identities would post 1309 proofs and burn roughly 68 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
